title: Infrastructure: retrieval & RAG stack
purpose: This is the offline-first retrieval core of the campus helpdesk. It ingests canonical Markdown/PDF knowledge into semantically chunked KnowledgeDocuments, embeds them into a local FAISS vector index plus a pure-Python BM25 keyword index, fuses both with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), reranks candidates with a local cross-encoder, deduplicates/merges context, computes a confidence assessment, and formats the surviving chunks into the LLM prompt context. It implements the retrieval adapters consumed by the application-layer RAGPipeline and RAGChatService, and the index-builder entry point run by `campus_helpdesk.ingest`.

files.purpose: Package marker for the RAG infrastructure subpackage; contains only the module docstring 'Adapters that implement the local RAG pipeline.'
files.notes: Empty package initializer; no imports or exports.

files.purpose: Pure-Python Okapi BM25 sparse keyword search store that scores KnowledgeDocuments against a query by exact word-term matching.

terms.definition: Okapi BM25, a classic sparse retrieval scoring function that ranks documents by exact keyword overlap using term frequency, document length normalization (parameters k1=1.5, b=0.75 here), and inverse document frequency.
The Lucene/Okapi formula weight that down-ranks common words; computed here as log(1 + (N - df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5)) per query token.
Keyword-based retrieval that matches literal word tokens rather than embedding similarity; here the BM25 half of the hybrid retriever.
BM25 scores are converted to a distance-like value 1/(1+score) so results share the SearchResult.distance interface used by the FAISS (L2) side and by downstream threshold logic.

files.notes: In-memory only; never persisted to disk. After a process restart the BM25 index must be repopulated (HybridRetriever.load rebuilds it from the loaded FAISS docstore). Distance values are pseudo-distances (see term), which are later mixed with FAISS L2 distances by the RRF fusion and confidence engine.

files.purpose: Production index builder that turns every .md file under data/canonical_markdown/ into chunks and FAISS/BM25 index entries, writing a detailed index-manifest.json for incremental rebuilds.

terms.definition: The trusted, curated source of truth documents under data/canonical_markdown/ from which the production index is built (as opposed to ad-hoc scraped or user-supplied files).
A JSON sidecar (index-manifest.json) recording build metadata, embedding configuration, and per-document SHA256 hashes used to skip unchanged files on incremental rebuilds.
Rebuild mode that compares each file's SHA256 hash against the previous manifest and skips re-embedding documents whose content did not change.
A SHA256 digest of the stripped file content used to detect unchanged vs. changed canonical documents between builds.

config: embedding metadata read from FAISSSimilarityStore._embedding_metadata (embedding_model, embedding_normalize)
files.notes: Called by src/campus_helpdesk/ingest.py (CLI entry `python -m campus_helpdesk.ingest` runs build_index(force_rebuild=True)). The manifest hardcodes embedding_dimension=384 and faiss_index_type='FAISS_FlatL2' regardless of the actual model, and reaches into private attributes of the similarity store (self.similarity_store._embedding_metadata, ._index_path). Skip/empty/failure accounting is returned as build_stats. Any doc that fails loading is skipped with a warning and counted in failed_documents, so a partial index can be silently built.

files.purpose: Deterministic, weighted confidence calculator that turns retrieved SearchResults into a ConfidenceAssessment (score, level, evidence breakdown, hallucination risk) without any LLM call.

terms.definition: A 0-1 composite of six weighted signals (reranker, distance, chunk count, source diversity, evidence consistency, citation quality) indicating how relevant the retrieved chunks are to the query.
A five-tier label ('Very High'/'High'/'Medium'/'Low'/'Very Low') derived by thresholds on the confidence score (high=0.80, medium=0.55, low=0.30).
A label derived from 1 minus the evidence-consistency signal, meant to flag when retrieved chunks contradict each other; here it does not detect fabricated facts.
Jaccard-style token-overlap of the retrieved chunks (shared tokens / total tokens), a cheap proxy for whether chunks corroborate one another.
Fraction of retrieved chunks containing a literal '[C' marker substring; a naive proxy for whether chunks carry citations.
A sigmoid over the top cross-encoder score (1/(1+exp(-score/2.5))) used when reranking ran, detected via an 'original_distance' metadata marker.
A 0-1 normalization (1 - distance/2, clamped) of the top retrieval distance; treats distance as FAISS L2 even though hybrid distances may be BM25 pseudo-distances.
Ratio of distinct source filenames to the number of retrieved chunks, rewarding answers that draw on multiple documents.

files.notes: Docstring documents an explicit limitation: it measures topical/semantic relevance only, NOT fact answerability (room/building numbers); fact checking is delegated downstream to services/answerability_engine.py and strict system prompts. The empty-results branch returns score 0.0, level 'Very Low', risk 'Very High'. Citation quality is a naive substring check for '[C'. Confidence levels are emitted as 'Low'/'Very Low' (title case); see PromptContextBuilder for a case-mismatch dead-code consequence. Private access to settings dicts; weights/thresholds are class-level Settings defaults, not env-overridable.

files.purpose: Post-retrieval deduplication and passage-merging stage that collapses '-dup' file pairs and text-similar chunks under a character budget before context is built.

terms.definition: Removal of near-identical retrieved chunks by filename normalization (strip '-dup' suffix) or by SequenceMatcher ratio above a configurable threshold (default 0.85).
A filename convention (e.g. 'admissions-dup.md') marking a document as a duplicate of its canonical sibling, which the composer collapses in favor of the non-dup version.
A maximum character total (settings default 3500) that stops the composer from accepting further chunks once exceeded.
Python difflib's 0-1 text similarity ratio used to decide whether two chunk texts are duplicates; a fast length-ratio pre-check short-circuits clearly different texts.

files.notes: Wired into the API in main.py, touch_app.py, and robot_main.py (instantiated with settings), and called from RAGChatService between retrieval and confidence evaluation. Constructor default max_context_size is 7000, but the Settings default context_composer_max_context_size is 3500 and wins when a settings object is passed — inconsistent defaults. Uses private metadata keys source/source_filename/parent_document to locate the source filename.

files.purpose: Reranks retrieval candidates with a local cross-encoder transformer (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2) scoring (query, chunk) pairs, with graceful fallback when the model is unavailable.

terms.definition: A sentence-transformer model that jointly encodes a query+document pair into a single relevance score, giving finer-grained relevance than the bi-encoder used for the FAISS index.
Re-scoring a short candidate list from the first-stage retrieval with a stronger but slower scorer and keeping the top_m (settings reranker_top_m=5) results.

Graceful degradation path when the reranker is disabled, fails to load (local_files_only with no cached model), or errors during predict: candidates are passed through un-reranked with a reranker_status stat ('disabled'/'fallback'/'error_fallback').

files.notes: Model loads with local_files_only=True, so it requires a pre-downloaded model; load failure is silent (warning log) and degrades to un-reranked pass-through — a quiet quality regression. Despite the name, _lazy_load_model is invoked from __init__ when enabled, so loading is eager at construction. On success it stamps document.metadata['original_distance'] (which the confidence engine uses to detect reranking) and sets distance = -score so higher relevance sorts as 'lower' distance. Constructor defaults (top_n=10, top_m=4) differ from Settings (reranker_top_n=20, reranker_top_m=5); the factory passes explicit values.

files.purpose: Dependency-injection factory that wires the configured embeddings, FAISS store, hybrid retriever, reranker, loaders, and chunkers into an application-layer RAGPipeline without starting ingestion.

terms.definition: Constructing and composing the concrete adapters (embeddings, stores, retrievers, reranker, loaders, chunkers) from a single Settings object and handing the assembled RAGPipeline to the application layer.

files.notes: Imports RAGPipeline from the application package — an upward dependency from infrastructure into application (layering inversion typical of an adapter factory). Uses getattr() with defaults for the newer candidate_window/final_top_k/rrf_k/weight_* /fusion_mode settings, and falls back to settings.reranker_top_n for the candidate window. If a persisted index exists it calls hybrid_retriever.load() and swallows failures with a warning, so a corrupt/mismatched index leaves the pipeline running degraded (BM25 and dense both empty -> RetrievalError at query time). Called from main.py's app factory.

files.purpose: FAISS-backed local similarity store (LangChain adapter) that adds/embeds chunks, searches by L2 distance, persists the index with a manifest, and refuses to load indexes it cannot verify.

terms.definition: A Facebook AI similarity search index of dense embedding vectors (built here through LangChain's FAISS vectorstore), queried with approximate or exact L2 distance.

The index-manifest.json sidecar that stores the embedding model name and normalize flag; _validate_manifest rejects an index whose configuration differs from the current settings (prevents loading a mismatched index).

Pickle-based index loading that can execute arbitrary code from a tampered index; FAISS gates it behind an explicit allow flag, and the load() method raises PermissionError unless faiss_allow_dangerous_deserialization is true.
A reentrant threading lock guarding add/search/save/load so the store is safe across concurrent request threads.

config: embedding_metadata dict (embedding_model, embedding_normalize) passed in via factory
files.notes: Dependencies: langchain_community.vectorstores.FAISS, langchain_core (Document, Embeddings). With the default faiss_allow_dangerous_deserialization=false the index is never loaded, so retrieval runs with no dense results (see risks). Note load() still hardcodes allow_dangerous_deserialization=True on the underlying FAISS.load_local call, but it is gated by the outer config check first. Metadata values are stringified ({str(key): str(value)}) on the way out of search/load. save() raises if the store is empty.

files.purpose: The hybrid retrieval engine that fuses BM25 sparse results and FAISS dense results via weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), applies source-prefix boosting, and returns fused SearchResults with diagnostic stats.

terms.definition: A rank-based fusion method: each result contributes weight/(rrf_k + rank) per ranker (here rrf_k=60, weights weight_dense/weight_sparse, default 0.5/0.5), and documents are sorted by the summed contributions.
Embedding-similarity retrieval via the FAISS store (L2 distance), the semantic half of the hybrid retriever.
A settings switch ('weighted_hybrid' default, plus 'dense_only' and 'bm25_only' shortcuts) selecting how BM25 and FAISS results are combined.
Hardcoded per-source-prefix score adjustments added to RRF scores: +0.035 for 'facilities/', '02-academics/', '03-admissions-fees/', -0.015 for '07-news-media/', '01-governance-policy/'.
Wall-clock milliseconds for the fused search, exposed (with per-rank rrf scores and snippets) in the stats dict used for diagnostics/evaluation.

config: constructor: bm25_top_k, dense_top_k, final_top_k (candidate_window/final_top_k from factory)
files.notes: Documents are deduplicated across rankers by SHA256 of stripped content, and each document's returned distance is the min of the contributing BM25 pseudo-distance and FAISS L2 — so the distance field is a heterogeneous mix that the confidence engine and any absolute distance threshold interpret as L2 (the settings comment documents that the old 2.0 threshold wrongly filtered valid results; the default is now 999.0). The source boost prefixes and +/-0.035/0.015 magnitudes are hardcoded magic values. BM25 index is rebuilt from the private LangChain store `_store.docstore._dict` after load() — fragile coupling. Raises RetrievalError when fusion yields zero results (e.g. index not loaded). Fusion shortcuts 'dense_only'/'bm25_only' bypass the weighted path.

files.purpose: Composite loader that routes a source file to the Markdown or PDF loader based on file extension, returning a list of KnowledgeDocuments.
files.notes: Thin router only; raises ValueError for any extension other than .md/.pdf. Used both by RAGPipeline.ingest_file and by CanonicalIndexBuilder during index builds.

files.purpose: Section-aware Markdown semantic chunker that parses Markdown into header/table/list/code/paragraph blocks, splits by heading sections, merges tiny chunks, and enriches each chunk with breadcrumb and department metadata.

terms.definition: A 'H1 > H2 > H3' heading chain prepended to each chunk's content and stored in metadata (chunk_meta['breadcrumb']) so both BM25 and the LLM see the document location.
A chunk bounded by heading boundaries; blocks within a section accumulate until target_chunk_chars (1500) is reached, then flush.
The Markdown heading depth (H1/H2/H3) tracked while scanning, recorded in chunk metadata and used to build the breadcrumb.
Classifying Markdown lines into typed blocks ('header', 'table', 'list', 'code', 'paragraph') so chunking never splits tables, lists, or code blocks mid-structure.

files.notes: chunk_size and chunk_overlap constructor parameters are accepted but never stored or used — dead parameters (the actual sizes are controlled by min/target/max_chunk_chars, which are NOT wired from settings; factory settings rag_chunk_size/rag_chunk_overlap are effectively ignored for Markdown). Department is inferred by keyword heuristics over filename/category/content (computer/cse -> CSE, ece/electronics -> ECE, etc.) with 'University Administration' fallback. Prepends '[Location: breadcrumb]\n# page_title - section_title' header to every chunk. Exposes module-level _infer_department as a free function.

files.purpose: Markdown loading adapter that reads a .md file, extracts YAML frontmatter metadata via MetadataExtractor, strips the frontmatter from the body, and returns one KnowledgeDocument per file.

terms.definition: The leading YAML metadata block (delimited by the MetadataExtractor's FRONTMATTER_PATTERN) describing a document; parsed into metadata and removed from the indexed body text.
Turning YAML frontmatter plus path info into the document.metadata mapping used later for citations, breadcrumbs, and source tracking.

files.notes: Path validation requires .md suffix, an existing file, and a size under knowledge_max_file_size_bytes (20 MB). Unlike pdf_loader, if the file is outside the knowledge root it silently falls back to the bare filename rather than raising. One KnowledgeDocument per Markdown file (chunking happens later). Depends on src/campus_helpdesk/infrastructure/knowledge/metadata_extractor.py.

files.purpose: PDF loading adapter that extracts text page-by-page with LangChain's PyPDFLoader and returns one KnowledgeDocument per non-empty page.

terms.definition: Each non-empty extracted page becomes its own KnowledgeDocument with page metadata and a 'source' entry, so a multi-page PDF yields multiple indexable chunks.

files.notes: Depends on langchain_community.document_loaders.PyPDFLoader and pypdf (PdfReadError handled). No OCR is configured: scanned/image-only PDFs raise ValueError('OCR is not configured for scanned PDFs'). Requires the file to be strictly inside the knowledge root (raises otherwise), which is stricter than the Markdown loader's fallback.

files.purpose: Formats retrieved SearchResults into a structured prompt context string with per-chunk citation headers (Source/Title/Section/URL), distance filtering, hash deduplication, and a character budget.

terms.definition:
The retrieved-knowledge string injected into the LLM system/user prompt, built as '[Source: ... | Title: ... | Section: ...]
<chunk>' blocks joined by '

---

'.
A maximum distance filter (default 999.0, i.e. effectively disabled) above which a match is excluded; sourced from settings.rag_distance_threshold by the chat service.
A maximum character count for the built context (3500 in the chat service); blocks are skipped once the budget is exceeded, except a single oversized first block is truncated to fit.
An anti-hallucination preamble ('[CONFIDENCE DIRECTIVE: LOW EVIDENCE CONFIDENCE]...') the builder prepends when the confidence assessment level is 'LOW' — currently unreachable (see notes).

files.notes: The constructor duck-types its first argument: it accepts an int, or any object with max_context_size / max_context_chars / max_context_length / similarity_threshold attributes. The low-confidence directive is dead code: it compares confidence_assessment.confidence_level == 'LOW' (all-caps) but ConfidenceEngine emits 'Low'/'Very Low' (title case), so the directive never fires — a real anti-hallucination guard that is silently inactive. Metadata header falls back to legacy LangChain keys 'Header 1'/'Header 2'/'Header 3'. If every match is filtered out, seen_hashes stays empty and the function returns '' (discarding any prepended low notice).

files.purpose: Composite format-aware chunker that routes Markdown documents (by extension or by '#' presence in the first 200 chars) to MarkdownSemanticChunker and everything else to RecursiveTextChunker.

terms.definition: A dispatcher wrapping the Markdown semantic chunker and the generic recursive text chunker so each document type gets an appropriate splitting strategy.
Aggregate counts/sizes (number_of_chunks, average/largest/smallest chunk size) computed by compute_chunk_statistics for build manifests and reports.

files.notes: chunk_size/chunk_overlap are forwarded to MarkdownSemanticChunker, which ignores them (see its notes), and to RecursiveTextChunker, which uses them. The markdown-routing heuristic ('.md' suffix OR '#' anywhere in the first 200 chars) can misroute plain text that merely contains a '#'.

files.purpose: LangChain Embeddings adapter that lazily loads a local SentenceTransformer model and produces embeddings with a manual per-text cache.

terms.definition: Dense numeric vectors representing text (here 384-d all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors) used for the FAISS similarity search.
The SentenceTransformer model is only instantiated on the first encode() call (guarded by an RLock), so importing the pipeline does not load the model.
An internal dict mapping exact text to its embedding so repeated queries/texts skip re-encoding; uncached texts are encoded in one batch call.

files.notes: Model loads with local_files_only=True and trust_remote_code=False, so the model must be pre-downloaded; if missing, encoding raises (unlike the reranker's silent fallback). The manual self._cache dict has no eviction/upper bound even though settings.cache_maxsize_embeddings=1_000_000 exists and is unused here (memory growth over a long-running process). _cached_encode (an lru_cache-based single-text encoder) is retained for legacy compatibility but is not called by the current code path.

files.purpose: Thin adapter over LangChain's RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter that splits KnowledgeDocuments into overlapping chunks while preserving metadata for citations.

terms.definition:
LangChain's chunking strategy that repeatedly splits on separators ('

', '
', ' ', '') until chunks fit chunk_size, with chunk_overlap for continuity.

files.notes: Depends on langchain_text_splitters.RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter; metadata keys are stringified on output. Used for PDF-derived chunks routed through SemanticDocumentChunker.

data_flow: BUILD TIME: the CLI entry `python -m campus_helpdesk.ingest` (src/campus_helpdesk/ingest.py) constructs CanonicalIndexBuilder(KnowledgeLoader, SemanticDocumentChunker, FAISSSimilarityStore) and calls build_index(force_rebuild=True). KnowledgeLoader routes each data/canonical_markdown/*.md to MarkdownKnowledgeLoader (frontmatter extraction via MetadataExtractor) or PDFKnowledgeLoader; SemanticDocumentChunker routes Markdown to MarkdownSemanticChunker (breadcrumb/heading-aware) and PDFs to RecursiveTextChunker; chunks are SHA256-compared against the previous index-manifest.json to skip unchanged files, then fed to FAISSSimilarityStore.add/save, which persists index.faiss/index.pkl plus index-manifest.json. RUNTIME: main.py's app factory calls factory.create_rag_pipeline(settings), which wires SentenceTransformerEmbeddings -> FAISSSimilarityStore -> HybridRetriever (+BM25SearchStore) -> CrossEncoderReranker -> application.RAGPipeline, and attempts hybrid_retriever.load() if an index exists. RAGChatService.respond (application) then calls RAGPipeline.search(query, limit, original_query): HybridRetriever.search_with_stats fuses BM25 + FAISS via weighted RRF with source-prefix boosting; RAGPipeline optionally reranks the candidates with the CrossEncoderReranker and dedups per source document; RAGChatService then runs ContextComposer.compose, ConfidenceEngine.evaluate (produces ConfidenceAssessment), and PromptContextBuilder.build_context (produces the context string with citation headers). The context string plus conversation history is injected into the Ollama LLM prompt, and CitationValidator post-checks the generated reply against the SearchResult documents. The same RAG pipeline (minus ConfidenceEngine/ContextComposer in some paths) is reused by the RAGChatService streaming path and by the robot/GUI entry points (touch_app.py, robot_main.py).
external_deps: Python stdlib (hashlib, difflib, math, re, threading.RLock, functools.lru_cache)
Local model files must be pre-downloaded for all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (both load with local_files_only=True)
risks: Index deserialization gate off by default: faiss_allow_dangerous_deserialization=false means load() raises PermissionError, so a fresh deploy runs without the FAISS index; HybridRetriever.search then has no dense results and (with no BM25 index) raises RetrievalError at query time. The pipeline silently degrades unless explicitly enabled.

Silent reranker degradation: CrossEncoderReranker loads with local_files_only=True and merely warns + falls back to un-reranked results on any load/predict failure, so reranking quality can silently drop with no user-visible error.

Dead anti-hallucination guard: PromptContextBuilder checks confidence_level == 'LOW' (all-caps) but ConfidenceEngine emits 'Low'/'Very Low' (title case); the low-confidence directive never fires, defeating an intended hallucination mitigation.

ConfidenceEngine measures topical relevance only, not fact answerability; high confidence does not imply the specific fact (room/building number) is present, and its distance signal treats hybrid distances (min of BM25 pseudo-distance and FAISS L2) as pure L2.

The known absolute distance-threshold trap: a 2.0 threshold wrongly filtered valid RRF/FAISS results and caused hallucination (documented in settings.py and config.yaml); the default is now 999.0, but .env.example still ships RAG_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD=2.0 (overridden by config.yaml, yet a stale trap for anyone relying on .env).

Hardcoded retrieval bias: HybridRetriever applies magic source-prefix boosts (+0.035 facilities/academics/admissions, -0.015 news-media/governance), and CanonicalIndexBuilder hardcodes embedding_dimension=384 / FAISS_FlatL2 in the manifest regardless of the actual model.
Layering inversion: factory.py imports RAGPipeline from the application package, making infrastructure depend on application.

Fragile private-API coupling: HybridRetriever.load rebuilds the BM25 index from LangChain's private `_store.docstore._dict`; upgrades of langchain-community can break it (failure is caught with a warning, leaving BM25 empty).

Unused/dead code and params: MarkdownSemanticChunker ignores chunk_size/chunk_overlap; settings.cache_maxsize_embeddings is never enforced by the unbounded embedding cache dict; SentenceTransformerEmbeddings._cached_encode (lru_cache) is dead; ConfidenceEngine._citation_quality is a naive '[C' substring check.

Model-missing hard failure path: if the embedding model is not cached locally, SentenceTransformerEmbeddings.encode raises (no graceful fallback), whereas the reranker degrades silently — inconsistent failure behavior.

Inconsistent config defaults: ContextComposer class default max_context_size=7000 vs Settings default context_composer_max_context_size=3500; CrossEncoderReranker defaults (top_n=10, top_m=4) vs Settings (20/5) — the factory overrides both, but direct instantiation is inconsistent.
CanonicalIndexBuilder skips failed documents with only a warning and still writes a partial index plus manifest, so a silently incomplete knowledge base is possible.
